posts.caption: Dad called it this morning: ice out on the cabin lake north of Ely, May 8. His spiral notebook goes back to 1987 and puts the average at May 6, so a hair late this year if anything. He reports it to the DNR every spring. Photo from his dock. 🧊🛶
Taylors Falls to Osceola with @owenbrandt.writes, who brought a sea kayak to a river trip and never once apologized. Eleven eagles by his count. 🦅

New to the shelf: Sigurd F. Olson, The Singing Wilderness, Knopf, 1956. First edition, first printing, signed by Olson on the front free endpaper, in a near-fine jacket. From an estate in Ely. Telephone the shop for particulars.
Woodpile's stacked, the stoves are drawing, and the harbor has gone quiet for the season. A few November weekends are still open. #grandmarais #northshore

Ice-out dates are in for all eight lakes and ponds we monitor. Every one opened ahead of its long-term median this spring, a few by more than two weeks. Lake-by-lake dates are on our website; link in bio.
Finally.

Three days at Tettegouche with Ingrid. Fog on Shovel Point every morning, the Baptism River loud below High Falls and one long afternoon on the rocks with nobody else in sight. Home now and still smelling like the campfire.

This morning's haul from Minnehaha Creek: two shopping carts, a road cone, a lawn chair, more cans than anyone wanted to count and one annoyed crayfish (released). Thanks to Ingrid and the neighbors who came out.
Cabin 3 last night with the stove going. Once the color crowds head home, November is the quietest month on the harbor and our favorite. A few weekends are still open; link in bio.

Our 2025 Water-Quality Report has been revised. A dilution-factor error in one contract-lab batch (25-0217, collected Feb. 3 through April 28, 2025) inflated open-water results at three Phase 1 sites: Corliss Lake, Penner Lake and Lake Odegaard. The errata are on page 3. If you have shared figures from the June edition, please use the revised numbers. Full report: link in bio.

Our lakes are getting SALTIER and the numbers prove it 🧂💧 Swipe ➡️ then do ONE thing this week: call or email your city council and ask about smart salting BEFORE the first snow!! Every pound we don't spread is a pound that never reaches a lake 🙌 chart: D.K. #SaltSmart #SaltWatchTC

media.description: View over the bow of a sea kayak on calm gray-green water in mid-May, shoreline trees just leafing out in pale spring green, overcast sky, paddle shaft resting across the cockpit

posts.caption: First paddle of the season. My hands remembered how. My shoulders are still thinking it over.

media.description: Curbside storm drain grate with a faded painted stencil reading DRAINS TO LAKE, a gritty line of leftover winter salt and sand along the gutter, fresh spring grass at the curb edge

posts.caption: The snow is GONE but the salt is NOT!! 🧂💧 A lot of last winter's salt washed down our storm drains this spring, and chloride doesn't break down or filter out. It stays in our lakes. Next winter starts with the choices we make NOW. Who's in?? #SaltSmart

media.description: Dark basalt cliffs of the St. Croix River Dalles rising straight from calm brown water, pines along the clifftops, the bow of a sea kayak in the lower foreground, bright June morning
Sea kayak pulled up on a sandy river beach below wooded bluffs, paddle laid across the cockpit, a water bottle stuck in the sand, early-summer green everywhere

posts.caption: Under the basalt walls of the Dalles this morning. Put in at Interstate State Park in Taylors Falls and let the St. Croix do most of the work. #stcroixriver #paddlemn

media.description: Wooden bookshop shelf filled with vintage hardcovers on Great Lakes shipping and shipwrecks, faded cloth spines and worn dust jackets, a brass reading lamp casting warm light

posts.caption: Newly arrived from an estate in Two Harbors: a shelf of Lake Superior maritime history, including several shipwreck accounts in near-fine dust jackets. Do telephone the shop if you would like a title set aside.

media.description: Wooden desk by a window with a folded paper map of canoe-country lakes, a spiral reporter's notebook, a pen and a half-finished mug of coffee in warm July afternoon light

posts.caption: Filed.

media.description: Early-morning fog lifting off a small Lake Superior harbor, a breakwater with a small white lighthouse, dark rocky shoreline and birches, pale gold sunrise light
The same harbor later in the morning under clear blue sky, Lake Superior glassy and perfectly calm beyond the breakwater

posts.caption: Fog on the harbor at sunrise. By eight it had burned off and the big lake was flat as a plate.

media.description: Road bike leaning against a low stone wall on a riverside parkway, the Mississippi River gorge and dense green August trees below, bright morning sun

Restaurant table crowded with bowls of curry, basmati rice and naan, a young woman with long light-brown hair laughing as she raises a mango lassi, a man with short graying brown hair in a chambray shirt beside her, warm evening light

posts.caption: Maren's home, so naturally we ended up at Gandhi Mahal. ❤️

media.description: Split Rock Lighthouse on its tall rock cliff, seen from a sea kayak on calm blue Lake Superior, kayak bow in the foreground, birch and spruce along the shore in late-summer light
Sea kayak pulled up on a beach of smooth round cobbles, a pair of neoprene paddling boots and a lunch sack on the rocks, Lake Superior stretching to the horizon under a hazy midday sky

posts.caption: Split Rock from the water. Superior stayed flat until about noon, then remembered it was Superior. Turned around under the lighthouse, ate lunch on a cobble beach with my boots off, and drove the whole way home grinning.

media.description: Torn bag of rock salt slumped in a garage corner next to a snow shovel and an empty bucket, warm late-summer evening light through the open garage door

posts.caption: Labor Day is almost here, which means plow contracts are getting signed!! Ask whoever clears your lot, your church or your HOA what their SALT plan is this winter. More salt is NOT safer, it just ends up in our lakes 💧🧂 #SaltSmart #MNwater

media.description: Training room with a dozen winter maintenance workers in work jackets watching a presenter beside a projected slide titled Smart Salting, a calibration bucket and a digital scale on the front table

posts.caption: Winter maintenance professionals: registration is now open for the district's fall Smart Salting training. The course is free for crews, property managers and contractors who work in the district, and it covers spreader calibration, pretreatment and application rates. Link in bio.

media.description: Two gray-haired men in a dark wooden booth at a British-style pub, one mid-story with his hands raised, the other shaking his head, pints of beer on the table, warm amber lighting and framed prints on the paneled wall

posts.caption: Ledger old-timers, back at Merlins Rest. Joel beat me here, as usual, and Ben is already arguing with him about election night.

media.description: Long picnic tables under an open park pavilion lined with casserole dishes and slow cookers and a single salad bowl, people in fleece jackets filling plates, maples turning orange behind the pavilion in early October

posts.caption: Season potluck with the Minnesota Paddlers at the Minnehaha Park pavilion. Nine hotdishes, one salad. Who's still paddling in November?

media.description: School library tables nearly cleared after a book fair, a few leftover paperbacks, folded display easels, empty rolling carts and a hand-lettered Thank you, readers banner, late-afternoon October light through tall windows

posts.caption: Book fair is packed up. Every child who wanted a book went home with one, and I would like a very long nap. ❤️📚
Glass-calm under Split Rock Lighthouse this morning. Superior doesn't hand out many days like this. #LakeSuperior #seakayaking
